besluite.fout: A new block opens with 'die hof' right after a block that also spoke of 'n ander hoër hof', so the referent is unclear and a reader can take it as any court.
besluite.rede: Naming the court the block is about removes the ambiguity, adds no new fact, and uses the protected form of the name.
'Nie een regter ... nie' is natural, emphatic Afrikaans and not a translation, so 'Geen regter' is only a lateral swap.

besluite.fout: The contrast 'nie 'n landdroshof nie' is tacked onto a long sentence right after 'hou,', so a reader can briefly misread it as negating 'hou'.
besluite.rede: A short sentence of its own says the same thing (a magistrate's court may not decide this) more clearly for a Grade 6 reader, and the plural 'daardie howe' in the next sentence still points to the higher courts.
